d.t: The yaupon holly, Ilex vomitoria, an evergreen holly shrub with white flowers and red or yellow berries, found in the south-eastern United States.
d.e: Yaupon is evergreen like the American holly and the familiar hollies of Christmas decorations, but the leaves of yaupon are small and smooth-edged rather than prickly. Easy to chew and blandly tasty, they would not stand out in a tossed salad.

d.t: A tea-like drink, "black drink", brewed from the leaves of this holly (or, sometimes, Ilex cassine).

d.t: The action of yawning; opening the mouth widely and taking a long, rather deep breath, often because one is tired or bored.
d.e: At length, quite exhausted by the attempt to be amused with her own book, which she had only chosen because it was the second volume of his, she gave a great yawn and said, “How pleasant it is to spend an evening in this way! […]”
